instruction: Make Alpha from Mesh (z-height map) The opened `scene.obj` is a button-shaped SubTool named 'Button': a flat disk of radius 0.5 BU and thickness 0.1 BU with a slight central dome of height 0.04 BU (total peak z = 0.14 BU). The disk sits with its flat bottom at z=0 and circular axis along +Z. Using the opened mesh in ZBrush, orient the view looking straight down the +Z axis at the button's top surface, and use Alpha > MakeAlphaFromMesh to bake a grayscale height map. Export it as a 512x512 single-channel PNG `C:\Users\user\Desktop\Button.png`, encoding the top-surface z-height per pixel (bright = tall, dark = no button). Requirements: - `C:\Users\user\Desktop\Button.png` exists, is parseable as a PNG of size 512x512. - Single-channel (grayscale) with bit-depth >= 8 (16-bit preferred). - Nonzero-pixel ratio (button footprint) in [0.30, 0.85]. - Foreground brightness std >= 10/255 (non-degenerate). - Pearson correlation between the PNG values and the synthetic z-heightfield >= 0.9.

command:
import ctypes, time
user32 = ctypes.windll.user32
EnumWindowsProc = ctypes.WINFUNCTYPE(ctypes.c_bool, ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_void_p)
EnumChildProc = ctypes.WINFUNCTYPE(ctypes.c_bool, ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_void_p)
def close_error():
    wins = []
    def wcb(hwnd, lparam):
        buf = ctypes.create_unicode_buffer(512)
        user32.GetWindowTextW(hwnd, buf, 512)
        if 'ZHomePage.exe' in buf.value and 'System Error' in buf.value:
            wins.append(hwnd)
        return True
    user32.EnumWindows(EnumWindowsProc(wcb), 0)
    for hwnd in wins:
        buttons = []
        def ccb(ch, lparam):
            text = ctypes.create_unicode_buffer(128)
            cls = ctypes.create_unicode_buffer(128)
            user32.GetWindowTextW(ch, text, 128)
            user32.GetClassNameW(ch, cls, 128)
            if text.value == 'OK' or cls.value == 'Button':
                buttons.append(ch)
            return True
        user32.EnumChildWindows(hwnd, EnumChildProc(ccb), 0)
        for ch in buttons:
            user32.SendMessageW(ch, 0x00F5, 0, 0)
time.sleep(95)
for _ in range(4):
    close_error()
    time.sleep(2)
